sentence: For a comparison at a similarly accessible entry point, this site\'s [guide to becoming a phlebotomist](/how-to-become-a-phlebotomist/) covers another allied health role with the same kind of low bar to entry: like pharmacy technicians, phlebotomists can start with just a high school diploma plus employer-provided on-the-job training where state rules allow it, though states may require an accredited training program, a license or certification, or other qualifications.

coreSummary: 'Phlebotomists typically enter the field through a postsecondary certificate program lasting less than a year, or through employer-provided on-the-job training after a high school diploma. BLS reports a median annual salary of $43,660 in May 2024 and projects 6% employment growth through 2034, with the training route and state requirements determining an individual candidate\'s schedule.',
'Unlike most healthcare roles on this site, phlebotomy does not have a single standard education requirement. The Bureau of Labor Statistics describes two distinct routes: a formal postsecondary certificate program (typically less than a year, offered through community colleges or vocational schools) covering anatomy, physiology, medical terminology, and hands-on blood-draw practice; or an alternative route starting with just a high school diploma, where the employer provides on-the-job training directly.',
'Which route makes more sense depends mostly on the local job market and state requirements. State requirements may include an accredited program, licensure, certification or other qualifications. A credential requirement alone does not establish that every state permits only the formal-program route. Employer-provided training remains an option where the employer and applicable rules allow it; its duration is not fixed nationally.',
'BLS notes that some employers prefer to hire phlebotomists who have earned professional certification from a recognized professional organization, and that requirements for that certification vary by certifying organization. Separately, some states impose their own requirement that phlebotomists complete an accredited training program or hold a license or certification. Organization-specific requirements may include education, clinical experience, an examination and practical components such as blood draws. BLS says some employers prefer professional certification; it does not quantify a hiring advantage or rank certifying routes.',
'According to BLS, the median annual phlebotomist salary was $43,660 in May 2024 ($20.99 an hour), one of the lower-paying roles covered on this site, without measuring the time or expense of entering it. Pay varies by setting: outpatient care centers paid the highest industry median tracked, at $48,450, ahead of medical and diagnostic laboratories ($45,700), hospitals ($41,490), physician offices ($40,480), and other ambulatory healthcare services ($39,180).',
'BLS projects 6% employment growth from 2024 to 2034, classified as faster than average, adding roughly 7,900 jobs over the decade. Phlebotomy provides direct patient-contact work. Further study in medical assisting, nursing or diagnostic imaging follows each program\'s own admission rules; the cited BLS profile does not establish lower training costs or an admissions advantage from previous phlebotomy experience.',
